chunks: And from him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The freed slave (manbuth) is free; if he wishes, he may make his wilayah (guardianship/lineage) for those who raised him, and if he wishes, for others.

key_terms.الْمَنْبُوذُ: A freed slave who has the choice to select his lineage/guardianship
key_terms.رَبَّوْهُ: Those who raised or nurtured him
key_terms.وَلَاءٌ: Lineage, guardianship, or manumission bond in Islamic jurisprudence

ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a manbuth regarding his lineage and guardianship after freedom?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadi’ (AS) clarifying that a *manbuth*—a slave manumitted by his master without a specific lineage attached—retains full autonomy to choose his *wilayah* (lineage/guardianship). This choice allows him to affiliate with those who raised him or any other group, thereby solidifying his social and legal status as a free person (*hur*) within the community structure.
